tool.name: upgradelab-runner
tool.authEnforcement: Enforced, not mocked: no authorization is present unless a named account signs it. Each call carries SorobanAuthorizationEntry values signed with ed25519 over the standard payload (network id, nonce, expiry, invocation); the host verifies the signature against the account's ledger entry (master weight 1) and consumes the nonce. mock_all_auths and mock_auths are never used. Single-key accounts only.

definition.name: vault-broken-upgrade-auth
definition.description: Broken v2: upgrade no longer requires the admin's authorization. Seeded on vault v1, upgraded with update_current_contract_wasm, then migrated.

ops.note: Attack on the OLD contract: anyone calls upgrade with no authorization. Must be rejected by the host.
The real upgrade: the admin signs the call; the contract calls update_current_contract_wasm.
Batched migration: convert at most 2 legacy balances.
Repeated migration call: must change nothing.
Attack on the NEW contract: no authorization at all, tries to roll the code back.
Attack on the NEW contract: mallory signs a valid authorization for herself, which is not the admin.
Repeated initialization by a stranger who authorizes her own call.

limits: Not a network: the compiled WASM runs in the Soroban host linked into this runner (soroban-sdk testutils Env). There is no consensus, no fees, no transaction envelope, no state archival or restore, and the host's protocol version may differ from the live network's.
Authorization is enforced with real ed25519 signatures over the standard payload for single-key accounts only; multi-signer accounts, thresholds and custom account contracts are not exercised.
State comes from the seed operations you wrote. Live ledger state is never cloned or fetched, and storage keys are not discovered: only the probes you name are read.
A pass means the named invariants held for this scenario's operations. It is not a proof that the migration is safe for all states or inputs, and not an audit.
Results from native SDK tests (if attached) are a different category from compiled-WASM execution and are never merged with it.
